source_text: Πεπλήρωται δὲ ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται τῶν παραπλησίων παραδόξων τῷ ἀναγραφέντι περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ παρὰ τῷ βαπτίσματι περὶ τῆς περιστερᾶς καὶ τῆς ἐξ οὐρανοῦ φωνῆς. σημεῖον δὲ οἶμαι τοῦ τότε ὀφθέντος ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐν εἴδει περιστερᾶς τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ παράδοξα γεγενημένα, ἅτινα διαβάλλων Κέλσος φησὶν αὐτὸν παρ᾿ Αἰγυπτίοις μεμαθηκότα πεποιηκέναι. καὶ οὐκ ἐκείνοις γε μόνοις χρήσομαι ἀλλὰ γὰρ κατὰ τὸ εἰκὸς καὶ οἷς οἱ ἀπόστολοι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πεποιήκασιν. οὐκ ἂν γὰρ χωρὶς δυνάμεων καὶ παραδόξων ἐκίνουν τοὺς καινῶν λόγων καὶ καινῶν μαθημάτων ἀκούοντας πρὸς τὸ καταλιπεῖν μὲν τὰ πάτρια παραδέξασθαι δὲ μετὰ κινδύνων τῶν μέχρι θανάτου τὰ τούτων μαθήματα. καὶ ἔτι ἴχνη τοῦ ἁγίου ἐκείνου πνεύματος, ὀφθέντος ἐν εἴδει περιστερᾶς, παρὰ Χριστιανοῖς σῴζεται. ἐξεπᾴδουσι δαίμονας καὶ πολλὰς ἰάσεις ἐπιτελοῦσι καὶ ὁρῶσί τινα κατὰ τὸ βούλημα τοῦ λόγου περὶ μελλόντων. κἂν χλευάσῃ δὲ Κέλσος τὸ λεχθησόμενον ἢ ὃν εἰσήγαγεν Ἰουδαῖον, ὅμως λελέξεται ὅτι πολλοὶ ὡσπερεὶ ἄκοντες προσεληλύθασι χριστιανισμῷ, πνεύματός τινος τρέψαντος αὐτῶν τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν αἰφνίδιον ἀπὸ τοῦ μισεῖν τὸν λόγον ἐπὶ τὸ ὑπεραποθανεῖν αὐτοῦ καὶ φαντασιώσαντος αὐτοὺς ὕπαρ ἢ ὄναρ. πολλὰ γὰρ καὶ τοιαῦτα ἱστορήσαμεν· ἅτινα ἐὰν γράφωμεν αὐτοὶ αὐτοῖς παρατυχόντες καὶ ἰδόντες. γέλωτα πλατὺν ὀφλήσομεν τοῖς ἀπίστοις, οἰομένοις ἡμᾶς ὁμοίως οἷς ὑπολαμβάνουσι ταῦτ᾿ ἀναπεπλακέναι καὶ αὐτοὺς πλάσσειν. ἀλλὰ γὰρ θεὸς μάρτυς τοῦ ἡμετέρου συνειδότος, βουλομένου οὐ διὰ ψευδῶν ἀπαγγελιῶν ἀλλὰ διά τινος ἐναργείας ποικίλης συνιστάνειν τὴν Ἰησοῦ θείαν διδασκαλίαν. ἐπεὶ δὲ Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν ὁ περὶ τοῦ ἀναγεγραμμένου ἁγίου πνεύματος κατεληλυθέναι ἐν εἴδει περιστερᾶς πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπορῶν, λεκτέον ἂν εἴη πρὸς αὐτόν· ὦ οὗτος, τίς ἐστιν ὁ ἐν τῷ Ἡσαΐᾳ λέγων· „καὶ νῦν κύριος ἀπέστειλέ με καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ;“ ἐν ῳ ἀμφιβόλου ὄντος τοῦ ῥητοῦ, πότερον ὁ πατὴρ καὶ τὸ ἄγιον πνεῦμα ἀπέστειλαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν, ἢ ὁ πατὴρ ἀπέστειλε τόν τε Χριστὸν καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, τὸ δεύτερόν ἐστιν ἀληθές. καὶ ἐπεὶ ἀπεστάλη ὁ σωτὴρ, εἶτα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ εἰρημένον ὑπὸ τοῦ προφήτου, ἐχρῆν δὲ τὴν τῆς προφητείας πλήρωσιν ἐγνῶσθαι καὶ τοῖς ἑξῆς· διὰ τοῦτο ἀνέγραψαν οἱ Ἰησοῦ μαθηταὶ τὸ γεγενημένον.
pass_a_gloss: The law and prophets have been fulfilled of the similar paradoxes to the written thing about Jesus by the baptism about the dove and the voice from heaven. And I think a sign of the then appeared Holy Spirit in the form of a dove the paradoxes having been done by Jesus, which things accusing Celsus says he having learned from Egyptians did. And I will not use only these but also according to what is likely and what the apostles of Jesus have done. For they would not have moved those hearing new words and new teachings to leave their ancestral customs and receive theirs with dangers up to death unless with powers and paradoxes. And still traces of that Holy Spirit appeared in the form of a dove are preserved among Christians. They cast out demons and perform many healings and see some things according to the will of the Word about future things. And even if Celsus mocks what will be said or the Jew he introduced, nevertheless it will be said that many as if unwilling have come to Christianity, some spirit having turned their ruling part suddenly from hating the Word to dying for it and having imagined them to be above or in a dream. For we have recorded many such things, which things if we write having encountered and seen them ourselves. We will gain wide ridicule from the unbelievers thinking us to be like those they suppose have fabricated these things and are deceiving themselves. But God is witness of our conscience willing not through false reports but through some clear manifestation to establish Jesus' divine teaching. And since the Jew is in doubt about the written Holy Spirit having come in the form of a dove to Jesus, it should be said to him: Oh this one, who is the one saying in Isaiah: 'And now the Lord has sent me and his Spirit?' In which it is ambiguous what is being said, whether the Father and the Holy Spirit sent Jesus or the Father sent both Christ and the Holy Spirit, the latter is true. And since the Savior was sent, then the Holy Spirit, so that what was said by the prophet might be fulfilled, it was necessary for the fulfillment of the prophecy to be known also to those who follow; therefore the disciples of Jesus wrote what happened.

pass_b_english: The Law and the Prophets have been fulfilled through paradoxes like those written about Jesus at his baptism — the dove and the voice from heaven. I take that appearance of the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove as a sign of the paradoxical deeds Jesus performed, deeds which Celsus accuses him of learning from the Egyptians. I will not rely on those alone, however, but also on what is likely and on what the apostles of Jesus have done. For they could not have moved people who heard new words and new teachings to abandon their ancestral customs and accept theirs with dangers up to death unless they did so with powers and paradoxes. Even now, traces of that Holy Spirit who appeared in the form of a dove are preserved among Christians. They cast out demons, perform many healings, and see certain things according to the will of the Word concerning future events. Even if Celsus mocks what will be said, or the Jew he introduces, it will still be said that many have come to Christianity as if unwillingly, some spirit having suddenly turned their ruling faculty from hating the Word to dying for it, and having imagined them to be either awake or in a dream. For we have recorded many such things, things we ourselves have encountered and seen; if we write them down, we will earn wide ridicule from unbelievers who think we are just like those they suppose have fabricated these things and deceive themselves. But God is witness to our conscience: we intend not to establish Jesus' divine teaching through false reports but through some clear, varied manifestation. Since the Jew is the one doubting the written account of the Holy Spirit descending in the form of a dove upon Jesus, one should say to him: "Tell me, who is the one speaking in Isaiah: 'And now the Lord has sent me and his Spirit'?" (Isaiah 48:16). In that passage the wording is ambiguous — whether the Father and the Holy Spirit sent Jesus, or the Father sent both Christ and the Holy Spirit — and the latter is true. Since the Savior was sent first, then the Holy Spirit, so that what the prophet said might be fulfilled, it was necessary that the fulfillment of the prophecy be known to those who came after; therefore the disciples of Jesus wrote down what happened.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal gloss, and Pass B provides a fluent translation that preserves all nuances, including the distinction between the Father and the Holy Spirit in the Isaiah passage. The scripture citation (Isaiah 48:16) in Pass B correctly identifies the verse alluded to in the Greek (Isaiah 48:16, though the Greek text itself only says 'in Isaiah').
